edits.old: The practical point of no return is a change in rollback feasibility, not simply the restart onto newer binaries. Raising featureCompatibilityVersion (FCV) enables features that persist data incompatible with the older release; MongoDB recommends a burn-in period before enabling them. Retaining the older FCV does not by itself guarantee a supported binary downgrade. (high confidence)
edits.new: Raising featureCompatibilityVersion (FCV) enables features that persist data incompatible with the older release, which complicates downgrade; MongoDB recommends a burn-in period before enabling them. Starting in MongoDB 7.0, binary downgrades are no longer supported for MongoDB Community Edition, so retaining the older FCV does not by itself make a binary downgrade supported there. In Atlas, an FCV pin is a short-term measure that does not simulate the behavior of the previous binary versions. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setFeatureCompatibilityVersion.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/5-changes-you-should-know-in-mongodb-7-0/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/major-version-downgrade/

evidence.quote: Enabling backwards-incompatible features can complicate the downgrade process since you must remove any persisted backwards-incompatible features before you downgrade.
After upgrading, allow your deployment to run without enabling backwards-incompatible features for a burn-in period. Enable these features only after you are confident that a downgrade is unlikely.
Starting in MongoDB 7.0, binary downgrades are no longer supported for MongoDB Community Edition.
doesn't simulate the behavior of the previous binary versions. It only postpones upgrading certain internal data structures that allow new server features.

edits.rationale: MongoDB docs confirm that enabling backwards-incompatible features complicates downgrade and that a burn-in period is recommended. Percona, quoting upstream docs, states binary downgrades are unsupported for Community Edition from 7.0, and Atlas docs say an FCV pin does not simulate older binaries. The framing that the 'point of no return' is a change in rollback feasibility is interpretive, and the 'does not by itself guarantee' point is scoped to 7.0+ Community Edition.

edits.old: Unsupported does not necessarily mean technically impossible: Percona demonstrated an older-binary restart after lowering FCV in its 7.0-era test, and a separate practitioner examined 8.0-to-7.0 FCV downgrade mechanics. Neither establishes a supported or universally safe production rollback procedure. (medium confidence)

edits.old: A customer feedback submission dated 2023-10-29 reports a production outage after upgrading Atlas to MongoDB 7.0 and says automatic FCV advancement prevented downgrade. This is an uncorroborated historical customer account. Current Atlas documentation describes a conditional mitigation: Atlas Core Dedicated clusters can pin FCV before upgrading; downgrade is limited to the matching previous major version, pins cannot exceed four weeks, and Latest Version With Auto Upgrades is excluded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
